Module 12: Publication II & Lightweight Commentary — Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, students will be able to:

  • Launch a zero-build 3-pane static TEI web edition on GitHub Pages (docs/: parallel facsimile <zone> overlays, switchable Diplomatic/Regularized/Interlinear reading views, and aligned translation).
  • Synchronize facsimile regions, source spans, click-for-parsing word popovers (.wpop with @xml:lang-keyed dictionary links), and English translations cleanly across panes with zero dangling # pointers.
  • Classify and draft concise, grounded scholarly commentary across three editorial categories: philological, historical, and intertextual.
  • Encode source-backed stand-off notes (<standOff><note target="#..." type="..." resp="...">) incorporating verbatim <quote> lemmas and verifiable <bibl>/<ref> citations checked by automated QA.
  • Audit and vet AI-generated commentary drafts under strict negative constraints, logging Accept/Revise/Reject verdicts and caught hallucinations honestly in EDITION_NOTES.md.
